cases.prompt: set up node and python version managers on my mac
install nvm and the latest LTS node
pyenv or uv? set up python properly on this machine
install java with jenv so i can switch jdk versions
install mise and manage my runtimes with it
i need multiple node versions for different projects
which version manager should i use in 2026 for python/node/java
set up poetry and pipx for python cli tools
my shell has nvm, mise AND asdf and everything is slow and conflicting - untangle it
npm install the dependencies for this project
create a venv for this repo and install requirements.txt
install pnpm and set up postgres for my web app
install homebrew
fix this python TypeError
set up android studio with the right JDK
upgrade all my installed tools
set up my whole mac from scratch for development
Set up version managers for Node, Python and Java on my Mac.
expected_behavior: detects existing managers first (nvm dir, pyenv, jenv, mise, asdf) and preserves what exists rather than stacking a second manager per runtime
on a fresh machine installs the modern set by default: mise for Node/Java/Go (node@lts, java@temurin LTS pin - noting plain temurin/java@latest tracks non-LTS) and uv for Python
adds mise activate and rustup PATH lines to .zshrc idempotently and enables mise's idiomatic version-file setting for node
respects an explicit user tool choice (asking for nvm gets nvm, per the classic reference)
verifies node -v / python or uv / java --version / go version in a fresh shell with exactly one manager per runtime

cases.prompt: python on this mac is a mess - system python, some brew pythons, nothing consistent. fix it with something modern
expected_behavior: recommends uv as the single Python tool (interpreters via uv python install, projects via uv init/add, CLIs via uv tool install replacing pipx) without uninstalling brew pythons that other formulae depend on
never touches or relies on system python, and explains why
notes uv self update only works for the standalone installer - brew installs update via brew
verifies with uv --version and uv python list

cases.prompt: i have nvm but also installed mise yesterday and now node is weird
expected_behavior: diagnoses the two-managers-one-runtime conflict via PATH/shim inspection (type -a node, which manager activates in .zshrc)
asks the user which to keep and cleanly disables the other for node (removes its init line or disables mise's node tool) - does not delete data without consent
verifies node resolves from exactly one manager afterwards

cases.prompt: give me java 21 and 25 side by side with easy switching
expected_behavior: installs both LTS JDKs via mise (java@temurin-21 and java@temurin-25) or versioned Temurin casks with jenv if jenv already manages java - not the unversioned temurin cask
sets a sensible global default and shows per-project switching (mise use java@... / jenv local)
